### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/types`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d62b649b32d6753615f343f0821ab4ef296276c8` — the merge of head `6a1dd2e1fd8926d82bc9fdac3e655519f874c44e` into base `94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d62b649b32d6753615f343f0821ab4ef296276c8 && git checkout d62b649b32d6753615f343f0821ab4ef296276c8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390 6a1dd2e1fd8926d82bc9fdac3e655519f874c44e && git checkout -B drift-repro 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390 && git merge --no-ff 6a1dd2e1fd8926d82bc9fdac3e655519f874c44e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 94d3e2543488fceda39fbfe88036bb6887037390` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Inputs: card #29374 body and all three comments (triage 6580463328, claim 6580761426, os-dev-report 6582133604); PR #29476 body, its 18-file list and the net diff; the check-runs on the head (all 65 completed at review time: 56 success, 8 skipped, 1 failure, `Check Changeset`). The recogniser's `--paths` on this file list decides no face (no schema, no governed path), so `hits` is empty and the Scope above lists every path of the diff plus the cited code; the brief asks for CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER and that is the tier served. The head's merge base with `main` is `0c640141`; the brief's `8ca9dd7b` is a later `main` commit (the PR's `base.sha`, and the base the CI job diffed the synthetic merge from), and the net diff is the same 18 files either way. `origin/main` moved after the head's merge; every cited file above is byte-identical between the head and current `main` except StudioDesignSurface.tsx (a later unrelated change, #29376), which was read at the head sha itself.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The accept set is unchanged — right.** No route, no schema, no permission and no envelope code moves. `ACTION_DISABLED` is still what `ObjectQL.describeDisabled` (action-activation.ts:317-319) is read for at both action doors, and `FLOW_DISABLED` is still what `describeDisabledFlow` (engine.ts:5206, body at subflow-guards.ts:54-62) is read for at the trigger, the direct run and the subflow guard; only the string `describeTurnedOffPackagedItem` returns changed. `ui/packages/core/src/utils/action-activation.ts` hides switched-off buttons from the served `disabledActions` names, never from the sentence, so no client parses the text.
- **The public surface that changes is the refusal message text, by kind — named right in the PR body and the changesets.** On the head, `WHERE.action` = `under Setup › Packaged Actions`, `WHERE.flow` = `in its package's Automations in Studio`, and the template is `This KIND is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again WHERE, MEANWHILE.` The action sentence is therefore "This action is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again under Setup › Packaged Actions, or you can use another action." and the flow sentence "This flow is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again in its package's Automations in Studio, or copy it there under a new name." Both are what the changesets and the checklist quote, byte for byte.
- **The MEANWHILE clauses are unchanged — right.** The action sentence still offers no clone (PackagedActionsSection.tsx header: no clone is chartered); the flow sentence still offers the copy.
- **The six pinned tests follow the producer — right.** types (byte-for-byte both kinds, plus a new `not.toContain('Packaged automation')` case per kind), objectql (byte-for-byte action), runtime door 1 (`toContain` of the new remedy), both dogfood pins (`toContain` of the new remedy; `expectDisabledSentence` still refuses the ledger name and any ADR), service-automation (`LEDGER_SENTENCE` and the execute-seam `toBe`, both byte-for-byte). The status-dimension check moved from `not.toContain('Packaged automation')` to `not.toContain('turn it on again')`: the status sentence is "Flow 'obsolete_flow' is disabled", so the check still separates the two dimensions, and it no longer depends on which page the remedy names — right, and stronger.
- **The checklist re-points are right.** api-backend `packaged-action-disabled-dispatch` acceptance[0] clause and verify and acceptance[6] verify now say `Setup › Packaged Actions`; automation `packaged-flow-disable-durable` acceptance[1] clause and its verbatim verify sentence and negative[3] now name the Studio Automations remedy; both TRANSITIONAL known gaps written by #29438 said they would be re-pointed "in the same change" as the producer, and are retired here with revision 13 and 10 history rows. The automation verify string equals the producer's output exactly. The revision-12 and revision-9 history rows keep the old spelling as history, which is what a history row is. `Lint & Repo Gates` (which carries the checklist shape gate) is green.
- **The doc comment on the producer no longer calls the page live — right**, and it states the two per-kind parts (WHERE, MEANWHILE) in agreement with the code below it.
- **The casing `Packaged Actions` matches the entry the reader sees**: the Setup sidebar label is `Packaged Actions` (setup-nav.contributions.ts:64, translations/en.ts:79); the page heading under it reads `Packaged actions` (PackagedActionsPage.tsx). The sidebar entry is what a person navigates by, so the sentence names the right spelling.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29374-turned-off-sentence-names-live-pages.md`: `'@objectstack/types': patch` — right. The diff publishes one changed string in `@objectstack/types`; `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/service-automation` re-read it from the dependency, and `.changeset/config.json` holds every one of them in the one `fixed` group with `updateInternalDependencies: patch`, so the consumers release with it. Nothing is added or removed from any public type.
- Clause-②: no — right, on the PR body and in the new changeset, with no `(narrowing)` arm. No declared capability is taken away at any consumer and no spec refusal is made real: the codes, the doors and the ordering are unchanged, and a machine reads the code. `Metadata-protocol: none` — right; `packages/spec` is untouched (item 4 is #29446).
- The two rewritten pending changesets keep their own frontmatter (27842: metadata-protocol, rest, objectql, runtime; 27966: service-automation, types, objectql) and their own `Clause-②:` lines; the PR changes one sentence of prose in each, no bump.

### ③ Boundary flags

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION — per sentence.** `Check Changeset` is red on the head and its log names exactly two rows, both `M` against the merge base: `.changeset/27842-disabled-actions-served.md` and `.changeset/27966-flow-disabled-plain-sentence.md`; the same log says the PR adds one declaring changeset and introduces no empty one. Neither row is a COLLISION: the files keep their card-numbered names and their whole bodies, and only a quoted sentence inside each changed. Both notes are still pending on `main` (no CHANGELOG carries the old sentence).

1. `27842-disabled-actions-served.md` line 15, the quoted action sentence.
   - Before: "This action is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again under Setup › Packaged automation, or you can use another action."
   - After: "This action is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again under Setup › Packaged Actions, or you can use another action."
   - The new sentence is true of the code at this head: `describeTurnedOffPackagedItem('action')` returns exactly it, and `ObjectQL.describeDisabled` returns that for the REST and MCP action doors, as the note's bullet says. The old sentence was falsified by this PR: the producer no longer emits `Packaged automation`, and the types test now pins its absence. Correction confirmed.
2. `27966-flow-disabled-plain-sentence.md` line 12, the lead-in clause.
   - Before: "A packaged flow switched off under Setup › Packaged automation is still refused `FLOW_DISABLED`, at every door that runs it"
   - After: "A packaged flow an administrator switched off is still refused `FLOW_DISABLED`, at every door that runs it"
   - The new clause is true at this head: the toggle door writes the ledger for packaged flows only (engine.ts:5676-5700), and `describeDisabledFlow` is read at the trigger, the direct run and the subflow guard. The old clause named the page ADR-0146 D11 retired; that was already false on the merge base (N-28, #28818, landed before this PR), so this PR does not falsify it, it corrects a clause that sits in the same bullet as the sentence it does falsify. Correction confirmed.
3. `27966-flow-disabled-plain-sentence.md` line 12, the quoted flow sentence.
   - Before: "This flow is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again under Setup › Packaged automation, or copy it there under a new name."
   - After: "This flow is turned off for this deployment. An administrator can turn it on again in its package's Automations in Studio, or copy it there under a new name."
   - The new sentence is true at this head: `describeTurnedOffPackagedItem('flow')` returns exactly it, and `describeDisabledFlow` (subflow-guards.ts:58) returns that for a ledger-disabled flow. Where it sends people is real, see ④. The old sentence was falsified by this PR. Correction confirmed.

So the answer to the dev report's open question is **A**: confirm the correction and land with `Check Changeset` red by design. B would publish, in the 18.3.0 CHANGELOG, a sentence naming a retired page as the one the product now serves.

**Other flags in the os-dev-report, answered:**
- `out_of_scope_findings` carrier #29446 for `.changeset/27842-disabled-actions-beside-item.md` and `protocol.zod.ts:755` (the `disabledActions` description still says "under Setup › Packaged automation" at this head and generates `content/docs/references/api/*.mdx`): agreed, that is item 4 and the card split it to #29446. It remains a wrong page in published reference docs until #29446 lands; escalated there, not here.
- `out_of_scope_findings` carrier none: the other pending changesets (28044, 27504, 27378, 27521, 29139) describe the old page as history, and `datasetCreate.tsx:17` names "Setup › Datasets" in a comment. Agreed: history is history, and code comments in `ui/packages/**` are the card's "Not here".
- NOT MEASURED locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): both ride `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Build Core`, green on the head.
- Dogfood: the CI matrix shards are `skipped` on this head (path-filtered) and the aggregate `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green; the two dogfood pins were run locally at `53a942ac` (18/18), the merge touched neither file nor the producer, and each edit is a `toContain` of a substring of the producer's exact output, so the pins cannot disagree with the code on this head.
- `Test Core` and `Test UI` shards, in progress when the dev reported: all now completed, success.
- The record's own sweep for the old sentence on the head finds it in nothing but history rows and the untouched `protocol.zod.ts:755`.

### ④ Design judgment

Does the new sentence send a person to a page that exists and does what the sentence says, per kind?

**Action — `Setup › Packaged Actions`: holds.** The Setup app's `group_apps` carries `nav_packaged_actions`, label `Packaged Actions`, component `automation:packaged-actions` (setup-nav.contributions.ts:64), bound to `PackagedActionsPage`, whose section does exactly one thing per packaged action: on/off for this deployment through the `sys_metadata_activation` ledger — the switch the refusal was written for. A `type: flow` action is switched there by its own name too (acceptance[6]). The sentence offers no clone, and the page has none.

**Flow — `its package's Automations in Studio`, and `copy it there under a new name`: holds.** The pillar is labelled `Automations` (StudioDesignSurface.tsx:491; `engine.studio.pillar.automations`). On an open flow of a read-only package with a served `_status` row, the header draws `FlowLedgerSwitch` (StudioDesignSurface.tsx:10669-10670, 10796), which flips the same ledger bit through `POST /automation/NAME/toggle`; a flow its pair overrides is switched by that row alone (#28570). The toggle door switches packaged flows only (engine.ts:5676-5700), and a packaged flow's package is read-only in Studio, so every flow that can carry the refusal has its switch where the sentence says. The copy is `New similar` in the flow's more-menu (`FlowItemMoreMenu`, drawn whenever `packageId !== null`, StudioDesignSurface.tsx:11250), the `POST /automation/NAME/clone` door with a new machine name and label, so "under a new name" is what the dialog asks for; it is disabled only when the caller cannot author metadata, with the reason in its title. A bookmark of the retired page lands on this pillar (`PackagedAutomationRedirect`, `packagedAutomationStudioPath`). Attempts to break it: a flow with no served `_status` row shows no ledger switch, but such a flow has no ledger row and so never carries this refusal; a package-less flow is never ledger-disabled (the toggle door refuses it by name) and gets the status sentence instead; for a read-only base the copy lands in the paired `.custom` package, which the dialog says (`bodyPair`) — "copy it there" still names the door the person uses.

**The docs pages, against the code they now cite** (prose, read for agreement only): Position Holders and Permission Set Assignment are `nav_position_holders` and `nav_permission_set_assignment` in `group_people_org`, label `People & Organization` (security-plugin.ts:1652-1656, setup.app.ts:67-69); the Studio item page links to them instead of drawing the sections (`SetupAssignmentsLink`). Position Holders' Add writes `user_id` and `position` only (PositionHoldersSection.tsx:274), so "no business-unit anchor" is true, and `sys_user_position.business_unit_id` exists (sys-user-position.object.ts:99). The catalog and the on/off switch of a position or a set are in Studio's `All metadata` area (`/studio/~all/metadata/...`, `STUDIO_ALL_PACKAGES_SEGMENT = '~all'`; security-plugin.ts comment: switched on its own page, a capability has no switch), and the old Setup address redirects there (`setupMetadataStudioPath`), the same wording permission-sets.mdx:385-387 already carried. The matrix editor's When column, the capabilities tab and the Delegated Admin Scope facet are all on that Studio editor (PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:497, 3467; PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx:48-50). Sharing rules and record shares stay under Setup › Access Control (sharing-plugin.ts:668-672), so the row left alone is right. Datasets: no Setup entry names them; Studio lists them (`nav_datasets`, studio.app.ts:210) and the All metadata area edits the dataset's page.

**Findings**

- should-fix — `.changeset/27966-flow-disabled-plain-sentence.md` line 13, the unchanged last bullet, still says "Only the last clause differs: a flow can be copied under a new name, and an action cannot". At this head the two sentences differ in two clauses, WHERE and MEANWHILE (the producer's own doc comment says so). The PR's stated reason for touching these notes is that the 18.3.0 CHANGELOG must not publish a sentence the PR made false; this one is such a sentence, one line below the two it rewrote. One phrase fixes it ("The where clause and the last clause differ"). It names no page and sends nobody anywhere, so it is not a must-fix.
- should-fix — `content/docs/permissions/administrator-guide.mdx` Step 3 says "create the User Position row directly with its business unit" without naming where that is done. The card asks each step to say where the task is done today; the place is the user's record page, Positions tab, whose New opens the assignment form with `business_unit_id` (sys-user.page.ts:245-265). Naming it is one clause.

No must-fix.

## 席位核对

**ACCEPT** · `domain:devx#1` · head `6a1dd2e1fd8926d82bc9fdac3e655519f874c44e` · 2026-11-02T17:00Z

1. **Shape:** 18 files (+100 / -58): the sentence in `packages/types/src/packaged-item-turned-off.ts` and its test, five pinned tests elsewhere, six `content/docs` pages, the two checklist items `api-backend.packaged-action-disabled-dispatch` (rev 13) and `automation.packaged-flow-disable-durable` (rev 10) with their TRANSITIONAL knownGaps retired, a new patch changeset, and the two pending changesets `27842-disabled-actions-served.md` and `27966-flow-disabled-plain-sentence.md`.
